title: introduce-ci-dependency-coordinator-and-fastpath-lint-lane
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: CI feedback latency has been increasing as dependency upgrades, monorepo-wide lint runs, and full integration tests run for small focused changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'dependency-coordinator' job that centralizes dependency-bump orchestration and a fastpath lint lane to give engineers quick feedback for localized edits. Goals: 1) reduce developer wall-time for common changes, 2) make dependency upgrades non-blocking by separating coordination and artifact creation, 3) improve signal-to-noise for lint failures by scoping fast failures to touched packages and running the full lint in a slower gated lane, and 4) tighten action pinning for release hooks.

What this PR does: - Add a new CI job workflow: .github/workflows/ci-dep-coordinator.yml that runs weekly and on demand to batch compatible dependency upgrades, create curated PRs, and publish a coordination manifest picked up by downstream CI lanes. The coordinator does not merge but posts a Linear ticket suggestion and a release-note draft. - Introduce fastpath lint lane: .github/workflows/lint-fastpath.yml which runs for changes limited by path filters (packages/*, sdk/*, docs/*). It runs eslint/ruff/format-checks and a lightweight type-checker. - Update existing lint workflow to run as lint-full.yml (nightly and pre-merge for high-risk PRs) that includes exhaustive checks and cross-package rules. - Change release automation: release-annotator action pinned to a specific sha with an updater that reads the coordination manifest to reduce false-positive release notes generated during batched upgrades. - Add caching/warmers: small prebuild job to fetch prebuilt toolchain artifacts and restore node/python caches earlier in the pipeline to reduce redundant installs for shard jobs. - Add documentation: docs/ci/README.md with contributor-facing guidance on when the coordinator will create PRs and how to opt out for single-package hotfixes. - Pin a handful of actions (setup-node, actions/cache, release-annotator) to SHAs and update lockfiles for the hermetic builder image.

Important notes: - No runtime code changes to product binaries. All edits are CI and tooling only. - The coordinator introduces a curated manifest under .ci/dep-coordinator/manifest.json; downstream jobs read it through a single artifact download step to minimize repeated network calls. - This PR intentionally narrows the fastpath lint to produce earlier, high-value feedback; teams touching multiple packages will still get the full lint. - There was one flaky integration test during validation; tests were rerun and all checks passed prior to merge.
commits: add: initial ci-dep-coordinator workflow + manifest writer
feat(lint): add lint-fastpath workflow with path filters and cache warming
chore(ci): pin release-annotator and setup-node actions to SHAs
docs: add docs/ci/README.md explaining coordinator behavior
ci: add prebuild cache-warmer job and update workflow dispatch inputs
ci_status: pass (one flaky integration rerun before green)
release_notes:
- Add dependency coordinator to batch safe dependency upgrades and surface suggested Linear tickets.
- Introduce lint-fastpath lane for quick per-package lint feedback.
- Pin critical GitHub actions to SHAs and add cache warmers to reduce CI wall-time.
review_conversation: Arjun: Can the coordinator produce per-package PRs instead of a single batched PR? Answer: design intentionally produces a curated batched PR with optional per-package splits; added opt-out flag to manifest.
Sofia: Suggest adding a TTL to the manifest artifact to avoid stale automation picks. Action: added a timestamp and expiry field and updated downstream download step to validate freshness.
Devon: CI image bump looks risky for on-prem private installs. Response: hermetic-builder bump limited to toolchain images used by CI only; documented change and added rollback switch.
Arjun: +1 after addressing manifest expiry and adding README guidance.
